Put the full name in 'name' and the email address in 'email'. If one of them is not present, use an empty string for it.

Today's date is 2024-05-19. I visited the CS conference website www.cs-conference.com. Here is the content of the page:

Use an empty string for anything that is not present on the page: - registration_fee: the registration fee amount shown on the page (as plain text, for example '150'). - payment_iban: the IBAN shown on the page to which the registration fee must be paid. - conference_name: the name of the conference. - start_date: the conference start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (the conference takes place in the future). - end_date: the conference end date in YYYY-MM-DD format. - location: the conference location/venue. - registration_details_url: if the page contains a link/URL leading to more registration details (for example a 'registration' or 'registration details' page), provide that URL; otherwise an empty string. - form_url: if the page contains a form for looking up the user's registration details, the URL of the page containing that form; otherwise an empty string. - form_field_1_id, form_field_2_id, form_field_3_id, form_field_4_id: the HTML input element IDs of the first (up to) four fields of that lookup form, in order. Use empty strings if there is no such form or if the form has fewer fields. - form_field_1_value, form_field_2_value, form_field_3_value, form_field_4_value: the values to enter into those form fields, taken from the user's account information above. Use empty strings where not applicable. Only report a form if the page clearly contains a form for looking up registration details (for example a form asking for an email address, a name, or a registration ID). Do not invent links, input IDs, or values that are not present in the page content or in the account information.
